VICENZA, Italy – California National Guard members worked alongside Armed Forces of Nigeria partners during an engagement in Abuja, Nigeria, Aug. 15-22, integrating the California Military Department into the AFN's ongoing air-to-ground integration efforts.
By directly addressing AGI integration, this collaboration made substantial progress on the California Guard’s top priority with Nigeria, its partner in the National Guard’s State Partnership Program since 2006.
The primary objectives of this meeting involved assessing current capability gaps in integrating Nigeria’s joint terminal attack controllers — commonly referred to as “JTACs” — into combat operations, analyzing existing force generation and training pipelines, and developing a mutually beneficial, long-term partnership roadmap, as well as future training pathways.
JTACs operate on front lines in wartime scenarios, directing combat aircraft to provide close-air support and other offensive air operations. This collaborative event was a significant step forward in strengthening interoperability between the California Guard and the AFN.
“The engagement built working relationships among the California Guard, U.S. Embassy Abuja, the Nigerian military’s Air Warfare and Doctrine Centre, and Nigerian Air Force personnel while establishing shared training priorities,” said U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Daniel Kempf, commander of the 146th Logistics Readiness Squadron, 146th Airlift Wing, California Air National Guard. “We also set conditions for joint curriculum development, virtual instruction, in-person training and evaluator development, which will pave the way for further development and engagements,” Kempf said.
Nigeria’s Air Warfare and Doctrine Centre is the primary training institution responsible for certifying JTACs across its military. Once certified, the controllers report to active theater commands to support tactical operations. The AWDC oversees the standardization of training and continuous evaluation of its graduates, while also ensuring that those graduates maintain their skills.
“Working together, we identified JTAC training, sustainment and ground-force integration gaps, and we produced a roadmap for building a more capable, sustainable program,” Kempf said. “That program will also support safer operations and stronger civilian-harm mitigation, improving the AFN’s abilities as a regional security provider and a partner to the California National Guard.”
According to Kempf, the AFN intends to train and maintain a mission-appropriate level of certified JTACs for each of its active combat theaters to ensure a healthy operational rotation, while lowering risks faced by friendly forces and local populations. As of August 2026, the AWDC graduated two training cohorts toward meeting this long-term goal.
“While the California State Partnership Program can’t directly provide or procure operational military hardware, our capabilities are perfectly aligned to support training, curriculum development and institutional capacity building,” Kempf said. “We’ve already identified and agreed on key areas to drive long-term improvements.”
U.S. Africa Command leads “Flintlock” and “African Lion,” which are major, multinational training exercises that take place annually in Africa, focusing on improving security and cooperation with partner nations. Kempf explained that future training that further integrates the California Guard and AWDC personnel into regional exercise frameworks would involve these events, among others.
“Additional potential events include virtual ground force commander instruction, practical training in Maiduguri, Nigeria, advanced JTAC-evaluator training, as well as Nigerian JTAC and air-to-ground-integration refresher exchanges in California,” Kempf said.
Planning these training opportunities not only helps further develop working relationships between partners, they also prepare reaction forces for unexpected tasks, which can involve wartime scenarios or missions involving disaster response.
“In peacetime, we concentrate on training, doctrine, airspace management and civilian-harm mitigation,” Kempf said. “In combat or contingency operations, the focus in these engagements can improve air-to-ground coordination and reduce risks to friendly forces and civilians.”
Along with augmenting Nigerian readiness, Kempf emphasized how the engagement benefited the Golden State's warfighting trainers.
“This visit strengthened our own readiness by providing practical experience assessing a partner force’s doctrine, training pipeline, equipment limitations and security constraints,” Kempf said. “Continued engagements will provide further valuable context for the California Guard to analyze tactics, techniques and procedures currently used in active combat environments in the region.”

HOUSTON — ICE officers removed Christian Ruvalcaba-Salas, a 28-year-old criminal illegal alien and accused child rapist, to his home country of Mexico Oct. 16. He was granted conditional permanent resident status by the Biden administration.
“This dangerous criminal alien, who is accused of doing unspeakable things to an innocent child in Mexico, was able to use the immigration status that the Biden administration gave him to allegedly slip into Mexico, brutalize a helpless child and then flee back into the U.S. through the port of entry to evade prosecution,” said ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations Houston Field Office Director Bret Bradford. “That same status then allowed him to remain free in the community for years endangering public safety, despite the fact that he was wanted in Mexico for raping a child and had been arrested for numerous criminal offenses in the U.S. Thankfully, our officers were able to track him down after he attempted to flee and repatriate him to Mexico to face prosecution for his alleged crimes.”
Ruvalcaba-Salas was turned over to Mexican authorities to face prosecution for allegedly raping a child in Aguascalientes, Mexico, in 2022.
Ruvalcaba-Salas has been arrested for numerous crimes in the U.S., including assaulting a peace officer, unlawfully carrying a weapon, criminal trespass and twice for resisting arrest. On July 21, 2025, he pleaded no contest to resisting arrest and received deferred adjudication.
"Criminal illegal aliens who are child predators and sex offenders represent the very worst of the worst and they have no place in the United States,” said ICE Assistant Director of Public Affairs Micah Bock. “ICE will relentlessly pursue these violent predators and remove them, making our communities and neighborhoods safer and more secure.”
Ruvalcaba-Salas was admitted into the U.S. as a nonimmigrant in January 2020, near Laredo. Under the terms of his admission, he was required to leave the U.S. by July 6, 2020, but he failed to depart and remained in the U.S. illegally. On March 4, 2021, the Biden administration granted his petition for conditional permanent resident status. On March 28, 2023, the First Judicial District in the State of Aguascalientes, Mexico, issued a warrant calling for his arrest for allegedly raping a child on Nov. 24, 2022. While the U.S. does not track departures through the ports of entry to Mexico, U.S. Customs and Border Protection encountered him reentering the U.S. three days after the alleged rape on Nov. 27, 2022.
On May 20, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services denied his petition to remove conditions on his residence and terminated his conditional permanent resident status. He was thereafter placed in removal proceedings, and on July 7, an immigration judge ordered him removed from the U.S. in absentia. On Oct. 3, ICE officers successfully tracked him down and took him into custody during a targeted enforcement operation in Giddings.

- Use or freeze perishable food items before the outage, if possible.
- Prepare ice packs or freeze containers of water in advance to help keep your refrigerator and freezer cooler for a longer duration.
- Fully charge all mobile phones, laptops, power banks, medical devices, and any other electronics.
- Unplug household electrical items (coffee makers, lamps, Alexa’s, fans etc.) and high value items (TVs, computers etc.) in the event of a power surge(s).

- Unplug sensitive electronic devices to protect them from potential power surges when the electricity returns.
- Keep one light on to indicate when the power has come back.
- Utilize battery-operated lights whenever feasible.
- Check in with neighbors who might need extra help, especially elderly individuals or Families with special requirements.
Once Power is Restored:
- Reconnect electronics only after the power has stabilized.

WASHINGTON — Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle traveled to Arkansas, Oct. 29 to 30, to meet with leaders at Pine Bluff Arsenal, Walmart’s corporate headquarters, and the University of Arkansas. Telle’s visit was an opportunity to move from discussion to action as the Army pushes to modernize the defense and organic industrial base, strengthen its global supply chain and build the intellectual and human capital required to ensure the U.S. Army remains the world’s most dominant land force.
The visit connected the Army’s modernization priorities with commercial industry and premier academic institutions. In his recent keynote address at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting, Telle emphasized that the Army must "evolve at the speed of business" and build a "seamless, frictionless, symbiotic relationship with American ingenuity." This trip put that vision into action across the Natural State.
"The forward momentum we saw across Arkansas wouldn't be possible without the leadership and advocacy of President Trump, Secretary of War Hegseth, Senator Boozman, Senator Cotton, Congressman Womack and the entire Arkansas delegation," said Telle. "They are backing our warfighters with the resourcing and legislative firepower needed to modernize our organic industrial base and supercharge our installations. That’s how we empower our Soldiers with every competitive advantage when they step onto the battlefield."
Forging "America’s Arsenal" at Pine Bluff
A key focus of the trip was Pine Bluff Arsenal, a pillar of the Army’s organic industrial base for more than 85 years. PBA provides specialized manufacturing capabilities found nowhere else in the nation. It serves as the nation’s sole-source producer of vital white phosphorus munitions and a primary manufacturer of tactical smoke, pyrotechnics, and illumination rounds. In addition, PBA is a designated Center of Industrial and Technical Excellence for non-lethal ammunition, chemical and biological defense equipment, collective protection filtration, and textile manufacturing.
During his tour of PBA's sprawling 15,000-acre footprint housing over 500 buildings and more than one million square feet of explosive storage, Telle reviewed the facility’s ongoing transformation, which supports the Department of War’s “Arsenal of Freedom” initiative to revitalize America’s defense and organic industrial base.
PBA launched its comprehensive ARSENAL READY campaign last year. The initiative transitions the installation from a reactive sustainment depot into the "Arsenal of Tomorrow" – a continuously loaded, modernized, multi-capability defense industrial park powered by public-private partnerships, expanded enhanced use leasing and portfolio diversification.
"Across the Army – the foundation of the Joint Force – we are committed to rebuilding our military and achieving peace through strength, and that begins right here in Pine Bluff," Telle said. "Pine Bluff Arsenal is 'America’s Arsenal.' What the workforce is doing here to shed legacy acquisition models and transition into a continuously operating, modernized hub is fundamental to Army lethality and our continued dominance on the battlefield."
Unleashing Commercial Logistics in Bentonville
In Bentonville, Telle met with leaders at Walmart’s corporate headquarters and visited their Global Security Operations Center for an open dialogue on how large-scale, globally dispersed enterprises maintain real-time situational awareness, operational resilience and rapid adaptability.
The discussion highlighted how both the Army and the private-sector could share lessons on managing complex global supply chains through natural disasters, dynamic security conditions and emerging global events. Maintaining this continuous operational picture enables organizations to proactively anticipate disruptions, adapt on the fly and surge vital resources to teams in the field – whether supporting communities in times of need or projecting sustainment across complex theaters.
Telle noted that as the Army works to enable endurance as the foundation for the joint force, having open exchanges with private-sector leaders provides invaluable perspectives on supply chain resilience and crisis response. This discussion demonstrated the Army's ongoing drive to engage with and learn from American commercial industry at all levels, adopting best practices that ultimately empower the warfighter.
Advanced Materials, Semiconductor Innovation and Supply Chain Leadership in Fayetteville
The trip concluded in Fayetteville at the University of Arkansas, an academic leader in supply chain management, contested logistics and advanced materials research.
At the university's Engineering Research Center, Telle met with academic leaders and researchers from both the College of Engineering and the College of Business. The dialogue focused on the critical necessity of cultivating future leaders versed in modern supply chain disciplines, expanding cross-sector engagement with industry and leveraging academic expertise to solve complex operational sustainment challenges for the warfighter.
“If we are going to become more efficient, effective and ultimately dominant on the battlefield, we must fully harness what we already have in America, which is the amazing spirit of ingenuity in our entrepreneurial capital markets and world-class research institutions,” Telle said. “We see that on full display here in Northwest Arkansas.”
Telle then visited the university’s Multi-User Silicon Carbide Research and Fabrication Facility, which provides a national platform for advancing silicon carbide semiconductor fabrication and other critical technologies that can enhance next-generation defense systems.
The final stop of the tour was the university's Civil Engineering Research and Education Center, where the group saw cutting-edge advancements in defense-applicable infrastructure and rapid-deployment logistics. They observed a demonstration of CEREC's groundbreaking large-scale structural testing and learned about its pioneering research into 3D-printed structures, fast-setting cement, and other advancements that support a stronger organic industrial base and more resilient supply chains.
"Under the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Hegseth, we are adopting a whole-of-nation approach to defense," Telle said. "From the vital production lines at Pine Bluff, to the global distribution engine of Walmart, to the world-class logistics and materials research at the University of Arkansas, this visit demonstrated the total national ecosystem required to secure our nation. By uniting military capability, private enterprise, and academic innovation, we guarantee the American Soldier is never in a fair fight."
title: Acting Army Secretary visits Arkansas to strengthen industrial base, forge partnerships

Honors Life of Darren Drake on Ninth Anniversary of Terror Attack

NEW MILFORD, NJ — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined the Darren Drake Foundation and the Drake family at New Milford High School for a special memorial flag-raising ceremony to commemorate the life of Darren Drake and highlight Gottheimer’s bipartisan Darren Drake Act, which was signed into law to help combat lone-wolf terror attacks.
Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.
“It’s hard to believe that it’s been nine years since New Milford and the Drakes lost Darren. A blink of an eye. Yet, as we promised then, we would always honor Darren’s memory. This community has never forgotten,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “The Darren Drake Act has become an essential tool in our arsenal to eradicate terrorist threats in our country. And, it exists because of Jimmy and Barbara – and Darren.”
Gottheimer’s bipartisan Darren Drake Act, signed into law in December 2022, helps stop terrorists from easily acquiring trucks and other vehicles to use as weapons in attacks. Working closely with vehicle rental companies and in consultation with federal, state, and local law enforcement, the legislation requires the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to take concrete steps to stop known terrorists from renting vehicles.
On October 31, 2017, Darren was murdered in a terrorist attack while on a New York City bike path, where he was deliberately run down by an ISIS sympathizer in a rented pickup truck. The Darren Drake Foundation was created to honor his legacy and pursue the ideals and vision he was so passionate about.
Gottheimer was joined by Mayor Michael Putrino, Councilman Matthew Seymour, and Councilman Arthur Zeilner.

Wanted Fugitive Tracked to Dominica, Arrested and Extradited Back to the Virgin Islands After Almost Two Years on the Run
For immediate release
Rashawn Abraham, Deputy U.S. Marshal
ST. THOMAS, V.I. – A St. Thomas man wanted for 12 firearm and drug related charges apprehended in Dominica and extradited to the Virgin Islands by the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS).
Jahi Grant, 46, wanted by the Virgin Islands Police Department (VIPD) for multiple charges, including possession of an unlicensed machine gun, assault on a law enforcement officer and possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, was arrested on Aug. 27 in Dominica by the Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force (CDPF).
Grant’s charges stem from a Dec. 2024 incident, where a machine gun and pistol were recovered. Grant fled the scene and a warrant was subsequently issued for his arrest in Jan. 2025.
On Jan. 14, 2025, the VIPD requested the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Florida/Caribbean Regional Fugitive Task Force in the District of the Virgin Islands in locating and apprehending Grant.
Through investigative efforts, community assistance and VIPD and USMS collaboration, it was revealed that Grant fled St. Thomas and was residing in Dominica. With the support of the USMS Jamaican Foreign Field Office, contact was made with the CDPF, alerting them to intel indicating Grant’s presence in Dominica and his active warrants out of the Virgin Islands.
On Oct. 19, 2026, CDPF Task Force members confirmed seeing Grant. He was taken into custody on Oct. 27, by the CDPF and officially deported and extradited back to the Virgin Islands by U.S. Marshals on Oct. 30.
Once arriving in St. Thomas, Grant was turned over to the VIPD and booked in the Virgin Islands Bureau of Corrections.
“This successful operation highlights the strength of our law enforcement partnerships throughout the Caribbean, “ said Kwesi R. Howard, U.S. Marshal of the District of the Virgin Islands. “I commend the Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force for their professionalism and cooperation in helping return this fugitive to the Virgin Islands. Working alongside the VIPD and our regional partners, we remain committed to ensuring that those who flee justice are held accountable.”
title: Wanted Fugitive Tracked to Dominica, Arrested and Extradited Back to the Virgin Islands After Almost Two Years on the Run | U.S. Marshals Service

On All Saints’ Day, I join Christians across our Nation in honoring the men and women through the centuries whose extraordinary lives of faithfulness reveal the great goodness and love to which human beings can aspire.
Every generation of Americans has understood the profound power of the example of a heroic and holy life, which is why the names of saints are so interwoven throughout the American landscape. We have San Francisco, California, named for Saint Francis of Assisi; San Antonio, Texas, named for Saint Anthony of Padua; St. Louis, Missouri, named for a saintly king of France; and St. Paul, Minnesota, named for the great Apostle. From Santa Monica, California, to St. Augustine, Florida, saints greet us on maps and road signs across the country.
Saints are just as present in the institutions we know and trust. Families turn to St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital when a child is gravely ill. Young Americans study at Saint John’s University, Saint Louis University, Saint Bonaventure University, and many other colleges and universities named for saints. Every March, millions of Americans celebrate Saint Patrick’s Day with parades, music, and the wearing of green.
Even our professional sports carry this legacy. When New Orleans received its National Football League franchise on November 1, 1966, the date was no accident: It was All Saints’ Day. A local businessman championed the name “Saints,” inspired by the city’s celebrated jazz anthem, “When the Saints Go Marching In.”
From sea to shining sea, these names are a constant reminder that a great civilization needs more than material success. It needs examples of goodness. It needs heroes not only of strength and achievement but also of mercy, sacrifice, humility, and love.
In the United States, we especially honor Saint Junípero Serra, who carried the Christian faith through the missions of California; Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton, who helped build Catholic education in America; Saint Katharine Drexel, who devoted her fortune and her life to educating and serving poor and impoverished communities; and Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, who established schools, orphanages, and hospitals, putting Christian charity into action and bringing the hope of Jesus to those most in need. Countless other saints—parents, teachers, nurses, workers, missionaries, and neighbors whose names history never recorded—quietly showed what holiness can look like in ordinary life.
All Saints’ Day proclaims a truth at the heart of the Christian faith: Death does not have the final word. Christians believe that through the death and Resurrection of Jesus Christ, the grave has been conquered and eternal life has been opened to all who believe in Him. The saints are witnesses to that promise. We honor them not merely as heroes of the past but also as signs of the hope that extends to every human life and reaches beyond our earthly existence.
On this All Saints’ Day, Melania and I offer our warmest greetings to all who observe this holy feast. I will always defend the freedom of Americans to express their faith openly and without fear. May the lives of the saints renew our gratitude for our Nation’s spiritual inheritance; strengthen our resolve to love and serve one another; and inspire us to live with the faith, courage, and charity that make a people—and a nation—forever great.
title: Presidential Message on All Saints’ Day

Coast Guard Southwest District interdicts 37 aliens off California, between Oct. 5-30
U.S. Coast Guard Southwest District Public Affairs: (206) 815-6689
SAN DIEGO — The Coast Guard apprehended 37 aliens off the coast of Southern California between Oct. 5 and 30.
On Oct. 9, a Coast Guard Maritime Safety and Security Team (MSST) boatcrew interdicted 13 suspected aliens aboard a 24-foot vessel approximately 7 miles off San Diego. The individuals were transferred to the custody of Imperial Beach Border Patrol agents at Ballast Point.
Later that same day, Coast Guard Sector Los Angeles-Long Beach watchstanders received notification that the crew of the Coast Guard Cutter Narwhal (WPB 87335) interdicted 23 suspected aliens aboard a 25-foot cuddy-cabin vessel near Santa Cruz Island while on patrol.
The Narwhal crew transported the suspected aliens to Coast Guard Base Los Angeles-Long Beach, where they were transferred to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP).  A Coast Guard Station Channel Islands crew seized the vessel and transferred it to CBP.
On Oct. 17, Coast Guard watchstanders detected a suspicious personal watercraft (PWC) traveling at high speed off Point Loma and diverted an MSST Honolulu boatcrew to investigate. When the operator failed to comply with the crew’s commands, a pursuit ensued, and Coast Guard PWCs were diverted to the pursuit to assist.
The vessel struck a wave and capsized during the pursuit. The boatcrew apprehended the passenger, while the operator swam ashore and evaded authorities.
The Coast Guard works closely with federal and international partners to disrupt human smuggling operations and ensure the safety of those at sea. Maritime smuggling attempts are inherently dangerous and often involve overloaded, unseaworthy vessels.
“These operations and interdictions reflect the Coast Guard’s persistent, multi-mission presence throughout Southern California’s maritime region,” said Coast Guard Capt. Jason Hagen, Southwest District chief of enforcement. “Our crews stand ready to conduct border security operations, enforce federal laws, and keep our waters safe. Dangerous and illegal migration attempts place lives at risk, especially when smugglers use overcrowded, poorly equipped vessels not suited for ocean conditions.”
-USCG-
title: Coast Guard Southwest District interdicts 37 aliens off California, between Oct. 5-30

Congressman Carter Releases Statement on Haley Stevens’ Break with Democrats and Endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers
Today, Congressman Carter released a statement following Haley Stevens’ endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race:
“In my opinion, Haley Stevens’s decision has more to do with a bruised ego than a commitment to the people she was elected to serve. I could not be more disappointed.
“I understand that losing a primary hurts. I also understand that policy disagreements can be deeply held. But when we seek public office, we accept a responsibility to put the people ahead of our own disappointment. That responsibility does not end when we lose an election or feel slighted by another candidate.
“Haley has chosen to endorse Republican Mike Rogers, whose Trump-style policies she once vehemently opposed. What changed for the families of Michigan? What changed about their need for affordable health care, good jobs, lower costs, and protection of their rights? Those needs remain, regardless of how she feels about the Democratic nominee.
“Antisemitism is serious, and we have an obligation to confront it. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has said clearly that he disagrees with the contents of the outside group’s advertisement.
“Michigan Democrats chose their nominee. Haley had every right to challenge him in the primary and to continue pressing him on policy. But endorsing his Republican opponent days before the election calls into question the convictions she asked voters to believe in throughout her campaign.
“I have worked with colleagues with whom I strongly disagree. Public service requires that. We cannot allow a personal grievance to outweigh the consequences of our decisions for millions of people.
I expected better from my colleague. The people who supported her, volunteered for her, and trusted her word deserved better, too.”
title: Congressman Carter Releases Statement on Haley Stevens’ Break with Democrats and Endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers

ASTANA, Kazakhstan – Two female freestyle wrestlers from the U.S. Army World Class Athlete Program embodied readiness and resiliency for Team USA during the United World Wrestling Senior World Championships.
And they played an important part of helping Team USA secure its first world championship for the first time since 1999 by edging powerhouse Japan, 137-135.
Spc. Adaugo Nwachukwu became the first WCAP Soldier-athlete to win a world championship since 2005 in a 12-11 thriller at 62 kilograms on Oct. 29 against two-time world champion and 2024 Olympic bronze medalist Nonoka Ozaki of Japan.
Sgt. Abby Nette dropped an 8-6 heartbreaker to India’s Manisha Bhanwala to earn a silver medal at 59 kilograms. Nwachukwu and Nette are the first women’s freestyle wrestlers in Army WCAP to win medals in the same world championships.
“I have a saying: ‘We’re not here to take part. We’re here to take over,’ ” said Bruce Robinson, Army WCAP women’s freestyle coach who assisted Team USA. “I say it jokingly but, at the same time. I’m not joking because I know the potential these women have. When they come into this program and develop the mindset that comes with being part of the military, it adds another layer to what they’re capable of doing.”
The success of Nwachukwu and Nette during the senior world championships also spotlights the opportunities WCAP offers aspiring leaders who want to compete at the international and Olympic level while serving the nation.
“The success has elevated the program,” Robinson said. “Everybody’s talking about WCAP now. I’ve gotten so many texts and messages from college coaches and wrestlers saying, ‘WCAP is killing it. What are you all doing?’ They see that WCAP produced two of the three finalists. Not everybody can say that. The entire year has been incredible, from having Pan American champions to having six make the finals at the U.S. Open.”
To cap off the incredible year, former WCAP stalwart Iris Smith will be inducted into the Nationnal Wrestling Hall of Fame.
The championship culture fostered under Robinson and assistant Nate Engel isn’t lost on Terry Steiner, head women’s freestyle wrestling coach for Team USA.
“They really transformed the program, and I’m glad to have Army WCAP as part of Team USA,” said Steiner, who has served as Team USA’s coach since 2004. “I can’t say enough about their leadership and what they have done.”
While winning the world championship is gratifying and a huge accomplishment, it’s not surprising, Nette said.
“This has been a long time coming, but at the same time, it just makes us hungry for more,” she said. “This is the first team title in 27 years, but it won’t be the last. Hopefully next year we continue building on it and keep setting the standard.”
Nwachukwu, the third seed, opened her tournament with two straight victories by technical superiority – defined as victories by a margin greater than 10 points – against Turkey’s Sevim Akbas and Sweden’s Sara Lindborg.
Nwachukwu beat Bulgaria’s Bilyana Dudova, ranked second in the world, 5-2 to punch her ticket to her first senior world final.
In the final, Nwachukwu stormed out to a 4-0 lead and led 9-4 at one point, but Ozaki scored seven straight points. Nwachukwu, who earned a silver medal in the Under-23 world championships almost two weeks ago in Las Vegas, overcame fatigue to score a takedown in the waning seconds.
The victory capped off a remarkable two weeks for Nwachukwu.
“I knew with U23 worlds and senior worlds so close together that I had signed up for a challenge,” Nwachukwu said. “Obviously, U23s didn’t go the way I wanted, but I had to leave that in the past. I knew I could win at that level, and I knew I was capable of winning senior worlds. I just kept telling myself to let go of the past and wrestle like it was my last opportunity.”
Nette, seeded fifth, also had a remarkable run. She opened with a pin over Burundi’s Gloria Niyonkuru, edged Russia’s Svetlana Lipatova 7-6, and pinned Ukraine’s Mariia Vynnyk, ranked No. 1 in the world, in the semifinals.
In her final, she led 6-0, but a questionable call changed the match’s momentum. That shift stressed the importance of having the proper mental mindset, Nette said.
“I had the match in the palm of my hand,” Nette said. “Watching Adaugo compete this past year and seeing how locked in she has been has shown me just how important that mental side is.”
As long as Nette and Nwachukwu are part of the program, something special is always going to happen, Engel said.
“These two are perfect examples of serving their country, competing at the highest level, and accomplishing great things,” he said.
Both Nette and Nwachukwu stressed it’s a privilege to compete at the highest level while serving.
“Whenever I’m working with kids, I tell then how fortunate I am to be able to do what I love while serving my country,” Nwachukwu said. “The Army provides countless opportunities.”
Nette echoed that sentiment.
“We get to represent the United States both as Soldiers and athletes,” she said. “That’s a really special feeling.”
The Army WCAP Greco-Roman team also had four Soldier-athletes compete for Team USA in the senior worlds. Sgt. Kamal Bey (82 kilograms) lost to China’s Halishan Bahejiang, 4-2; Sgt. Dalton Roberts (60 kilograms) lost to Romania’s Razvan Arnaut by technical superiority, 9-0; and Spc. Timothy Young (97 kilograms) lost to Croatia’s Matej Mandic, 4-3.
All were eliminated when their opponents failed to reach their respective finals.
title: U.S. Army WCAP women wrestlers make history, help Team USA capture first world title since 1999

SCHOFIELD BARRACKS, Hawaii – Combat credibility begins long before the first round is fired. It starts with disciplined preparation, setting the theater, and establishing the lines of communication necessary to fight and win in a complex archipelagic environment.
The division-level Combined Arms Rehearsal on Nov. 1, brought U.S. Army Soldiers of the 2nd Mobile Brigade, 25th Infantry Division, alongside joint and multinational partners, into the reception, staging, and onward integration phase of Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center (JPMRC) Rotation 27-01.
Before any troops move out to the training areas, commanders and international partners gathered to walk through the upcoming operation step-by-step. Building this shared understanding is the crucial first step to bring diverse forces from across the globe together into one cohesive team.
"Today’s rehearsal is a great opportunity to get everyone, to include our joint and foreign partners on the same page with what we plan to happen," said Maj. Gen. Jeff VanAntwerp, commanding general of the 25th Infantry Division and U.S. Army Hawaii.
VanAntwerp compared it to Mike Tyson famously saying that ‘everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face.’
He concluded that beyond understanding the plan, it’s important to understand the commander’s intent – the purpose, key tasks, and desired end state.
“[That] is the real objective. We expect the plan to change, and rehearsals like the one today help us adapt quickly to those changes to ensure that we still win,” said VanAntwerp
While the overarching strategy relies on convergence, the 2nd Mobile Brigade is actively preparing for the close battle. These Soldiers are gearing up to seize, retain, and exploit decisive terrain, on both Oahu and the Island of Hawaii.
"Our Soldiers are ready for the close battle," said Col. Ari Martyn, commander of the 2nd Mobile Brigade. "We are demonstrating our ability to fight, endure, and strike in the most demanding archipelagic and jungle environments on earth."
Behind the scenes of the arriving infantry battalions, a massive logistical network is already operating to sustain the force. At Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, U.S. Army riggers and logisticians with the 8th Theater Sustainment Command working seamlessly alongside both the 11th Airborne Division and our U.S. Marine Corps partners, rigging heavy equipment and container delivery systems for future airdrops and resupply.
"Endurance carries the fight across time and distance," said Lt. Col. Adan Cazarez, chief of public affairs for the 8th Theater Sustainment Command.
This unseen work builds the endurance required for distributed operations. By securing these critical supply lines, logisticians ensure the maneuver forces can project combat power and maintain a relentless tempo across the island chain.
"By integrating our aerial delivery and maritime transport capabilities with our joint partners early, we ensure the maneuver forces have the supplies they need to maintain continuous pressure throughout the exercise," said Cazarez
Over the coming days, this logistical backbone will expand the brigade's operational reach. Army watercraft, including logistics support vessels, are loading tactical vehicles at Waipio Point for maritime transit to the Big Island. Simultaneously, a joint airbridge is staging to rapidly push troops and critical payloads directly into Kona.
This distributed access and mobility sets the stage for the division's strike capabilities. With a secure network in place, the joint force is postured to rapidly deploy long-range precision fires, such as the High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS), and combat aviation assets to austere locations, extending the commander's reach.
Throughout November, JPMRC 27-01 brings together approximately 7,000 personnel, including allies and partners from Singapore, the Republic of Korea, France, New Zealand, Japan, and the Maldives. As forces finish their preparations and push toward the training areas for the beginning of force-on-force operations on Nov. 7, the focus remains on building a lethal, combat-ready force capable of operating seamlessly as one combined joint team of teams.
About the Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center:
The Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center is U.S. Army Pacific’s premier regional Combat Training Center. Operating across the Hawaiian Islands, Alaska, and exportable locations throughout the Indo-Pacific, JPMRC provides realistic, live, virtual, and constructive training in complex archipelagic, jungle, and arctic environments. The center generates combat-credible forces, validates multi-domain readiness, and deepens interoperability with Joint forces, allies, and multinational partners to uphold a free and open Indo-Pacific.
About the 25th Infantry Division:
The 25th Infantry Division, "Tropic Lightning," is America's Pacific Division, headquartered at Schofield Barracks, Hawaii. As the premier land force in the Pacific, the 25th ID provides combat-ready forces capable of conducting decisive operations across the Indo-Pacific. Through rigorous training and close partnerships with allies and the Joint Force, the division remains committed to warfighting excellence, regional stability, and being a responsible steward of the ‘āina and our local communities across the State of Hawaii.
title: Tropic Lightning, Joint Partners Set the Theater for JPMRC 27-01

Wanted Fugitive Arrested in Dominica Brought Back to Virgin Islands After Almost 2 Years on the Run
For immediate release
Rashawn Abraham, Deputy U.S. Marshal
ST. THOMAS, V.I. – AA St. Thomas man wanted on 12 firearm and drug related charges apprehended in Dominica has been brought back to the Virgin Islands by the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS).
Jahi Grant, 46, wanted by the Virgin Islands Police Department (VIPD) for multiple charges, including possession of an unlicensed machine gun, assault on a law enforcement officer and possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, was arrested on Oct. 27 in Dominica by the Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force (CDPF).
“This successful operation highlights the strength of our law enforcement partnerships throughout the Caribbean,” said Kwesi R. Howard, U.S. Marshal of the District of the Virgin Islands. “I commend the Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force for their professionalism and cooperation in helping return this fugitive to the Virgin Islands. Working alongside the VIPD and our regional partners, we remain committed to ensuring that those who flee justice are held accountable.”
Grant’s charges stem from a December 2024 incident, in which a machine gun and pistol were recovered. Grant fled the scene, and a warrant was subsequently issued for his arrest in January 2025.
On Jan. 14, 2025, the VIPD requested the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Florida/Caribbean Regional Fugitive Task Force in the District of the Virgin Islands in locating and apprehending Grant.
Investigators learned, through community assistance and VIPD and USMS collaboration, that Grant fled St. Thomas and was residing in Dominica. With the support of the USMS Jamaican Foreign Field Office, the CDPF was alerted to Grant’s presence in Dominica and his active warrants out of the Virgin Islands.
On Oct. 19, CDPF Task Force members confirmed seeing Grant. He was taken into custody on Oct. 27 by the CDPF and officially deported and repatriated to the Virgin Islands by U.S. Marshals on Oct. 30.
Once arriving in St. Thomas, Grant was turned over to the VIPD and booked in the Virgin Islands Bureau of Corrections.
title: Wanted Fugitive Arrested in Dominica Brought Back to Virgin Islands After Almost 2 Years on the Run | U.S. Marshals Service

Good Samaritan, Coast Guard rescue three boaters from vessel on fire off San Francisco
U.S. Coast Guard Southwest District Public Affairs: (206) 815-6689
SAN FRANCISCO — The Coast Guard and a good Samaritan vessel rescued three people Friday from a 32-foot motor vessel that was on fire and taking on water approximately 5 miles west of Stinson Beach.
Coast Guard Sector San Francisco watchstanders received a distress call on VHF channel 16 at 11:58 a.m. from a good Samaritan who reported smoke coming from the vessel and a person aboard waving their arms.
Watchstanders coordinated the launches of a Coast Guard Station Golden Gate 47-foot motor lifeboat crew and a Coast Guard Air Station San Francisco MH-65 Dolphin helicopter aircrew. Before Coast Guard crews arrived, the good Samaritan vessel rescued all three boaters from the vessel, which subsequently sank.
The Station Golden Gate crew arrived on scene and transferred the three boaters to the motor lifeboat. After determining none of the survivors required medical assistance, the crew transported them to Pier 45, their original point of departure.
The vessel’s master reported that the vessel began taking on water rapidly through the stern engine compartment before sinking.
The cause of the incident is currently under investigation.
-USCG-
title: Good Samaritan, Coast Guard rescue three boaters from vessel on fire off San Francisco

Congressman Carter Condemns Haley Stevens’ Break with Democrats and Endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers
Today, Congressman Carter released a statement following Haley Stevens’ endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race:
“In my opinion, Haley Stevens’s decision has more to do with a bruised ego than a commitment to the people she was elected to serve. I could not be more disappointed.
“I understand that losing a primary hurts. I also understand that policy disagreements can be deeply held. But when we seek public office, we accept a responsibility to put the people ahead of our own disappointment. That responsibility does not end when we lose an election or feel slighted by another candidate.
“Haley has chosen to endorse Republican Mike Rogers, whose Trump-style policies she once vehemently opposed. What changed for the families of Michigan? What changed about their need for affordable health care, good jobs, lower costs, and protection of their rights? Those needs remain, regardless of how she feels about the Democratic nominee.
“Antisemitism is serious, and we have an obligation to confront it. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has said clearly that he disagrees with the contents of the outside group’s advertisement.
“Michigan Democrats chose their nominee. Haley had every right to challenge him in the primary and to continue pressing him on policy. But endorsing his Republican opponent days before the election calls into question the convictions she asked voters to believe in throughout her campaign.
“I have worked with colleagues with whom I strongly disagree. Public service requires that. We cannot allow a personal grievance to outweigh the consequences of our decisions for millions of people.
I expected better from my colleague. The people who supported her, volunteered for her, and trusted her word deserved better, too.”
title: Congressman Carter Condemns Haley Stevens’ Break with Democrats and Endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers

Missing Teen from Garden City Safely Recovered in Oregon
On November 1, 2026, law enforcement in Oregon, working directly with FBI Salt Lake City and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office, safely recovered a 17-year-old teenage girl, who was reported missing from Garden City, Utah, in May 2025.
She was located this afternoon in Oregon with a 39-year-old male, who was taken into custody without incident.
“Tonight, local police in Oregon brought a minor who had been missing for a year and a half to safety, acting on information provided by our FBI Salt Lake City Field Office,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “We are grateful she can return home, and we will continue working with our partners to hold those responsible accountable. To anyone using gore groups to target and exploit children: the FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our 
disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice and protect America’s children.”
The FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the U.S. and in other countries. As this case is ongoing, no further information will be released at this time.
The FBI and Rich County Sheriff’s Office appreciate invaluable assistance from Oregon State Police, FBI Portland, and the Utah Department of Public Safety.
title: Missing Teen from Garden City Safely Recovered in Oregon

RELEASE: Gottheimer Joins North Jersey Families Helped With Military Pension Back Pay, Health Insurance Coverage, IRS Refunds, and More
Clawed Back More than $173 Million to Date; Solved a Total of 22,959 Cases to Date
Above: Gottheimer joins Jersey constituents.
HACKENSACK, NJ — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined North Jersey constituents, including veterans, seniors, nurses, and local families, to discuss how his office helped them receive benefits and services they were owed from federal agencies and private companies. Their cases included military pension back pay, health insurance coverage, identity theft, immigration paperwork, and delayed IRS refunds.
Gottheimer’s full remarks can be found here.
“One of the most important parts of my job is being an advocate and a champion for the families I’m lucky to represent here in North Jersey. By fighting for our Fifth District families, we’ve helped thousands of residents who’ve been denied Social Security checks, unemployment benefits, VA benefits, critical health care, tax refunds, or crucial resources they need, often because of bureaucratic red tape,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Whether it’s the IRS, an insurance company, or a federal agency that’s gotten it wrong, I’ll always fight for Jersey families across the Fifth District to get what they are owed and deserve. If you need help with any issues, including Medicare, Social Security, passports, VA benefits, and so much more, please reach out to me.”
In the last five years alone, Gottheimer’s office has helped more than 780 veterans access their VA benefits and service medals; more than 1,834 Fifth District seniors access their earned Social Security checks and claw back over $2.6 million from the Social Security Administration; get more than 65 constituents back home from being trapped overseas, including some stranded in Israel after October 7; more than 4,500 constituents get their unemployment benefits; and claw back over $120 million owed to small businesses, non-profits, and constituents from the IRS. In total, Gottheimer’s office has clawed back more than $173 million to date for constituents through its casework team. Just among the cases highlighted today, the office helped get back more than $171,000 for Fifth District families.
Gottheimer joined Fifth District residents today:
- Tom Gallagher of Mahwah: Tom’s brother, Retired Air Force Major John P. Gallagher, served in the U.S. Air Force for over 20 years and now lives in an assisted living facility after being diagnosed with early dementia. Tom holds power of attorney and looks out for him. For five months, Retired Major John’s pension was not being deposited because his bank account had been closed due to fraudulent and unauthorized withdrawals. Tom reached out to Gottheimer’s office for help working with the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), and Gottheimer’s team got right to work and contacted DFAS. The next day, DFAS processed John’s forms and placed his pension account back in active pay status. Within a week, DFAS confirmed the issue was resolved and that his brother’s back pay had been issued. In less than two weeks, Tom confirmed that his brother’s owed pension had received the gross pay he earned after waiting for five months.
- Suzanne Jackson of Highland Lakes: Suzanne is a registered nurse who has spent more than 40 years caring for patients at Englewood Hospital. This past July, she reached out to Gottheimer’s office after UnitedHealthcare denied coverage for a prosthetic limb, initially deeming it not medically necessary. Although her doctor said she qualified for a K3 prosthetic with a microprocessor knee, UnitedHealthcare only approved a K2 prosthetic after her first appeal, which meant she could not continue working 12-hour shifts as a nurse. After months of fighting the decision, and being unable to reach anyone at UnitedHealthcare to escalate her appeal, Suzanne turned to Gottheimer. His team contacted UnitedHealthcare and asked them to take another look. Just a day later, UnitedHealthcare approved the K3 prosthetic with a microprocessor knee, and Suzanne is still on the job at Englewood Hospital.
- Joey Shimm of Tenafly, on behalf of his wife, Yoko: Yoko’s green card arrived with a typo, an extra initial in her name, and the replacement came back with the very same mistake. When Yoko’s 95-year-old mother suffered a cerebral hemorrhage in Japan, Yoko needed a USCIS-approved travel document to get to her side, and the earliest appointment USCIS would offer was after her planned flight. Joey turned to Gottheimer’s office. His team immediately contacted the USCIS Newark Field Office Congressional Lead and secured an appointment for the very next day. Yoko received an ADIT stamp in her Japanese passport, which provides temporary proof of her lawful permanent resident status, and she traveled to Japan to be with her hospitalized mother. Gottheimer’s office will keep working with the family until the green card itself is fully corrected.
- Robert Lunzer of Englewood: For a year, money had been coming out of Robert’s monthly Social Security retirement benefit, and he had no idea why. It turned out to be from missing payments on a more than $93,000 Small Business Administration (SBA) COVID loan he never took out. The application didn’t even have his real name on it, only a signature he never signed, and the money was going to an offshore bank account. After two weeks of getting nowhere with the SBA, Robert called Gottheimer’s office. His team contacted the SBA the very next day, and the inquiry was sent to the SBA’s fraud unit. In just one week, the SBA validated Robert’s identity theft claim, forgave the entire $93,600 fraudulent debt, stopped the garnishment of his Social Security benefits, and refunded about $4,500 to him in a lump sum.
- Ann Marie and Jim Dunlop of Haworth: Ann Marie and Jim, both in their eighties, filed their taxes in mid-March, on time. The IRS told them to complete an ID verification over the phone, and then they never heard another word, aside from a letter every six weeks saying the IRS needed more time. Gottheimer’s team contacted the Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS), learned that the return was under review because of unverifiable income and withholding, and worked with Ann Marie and her accountant to gather the records needed to verify her withholding. Gottheimer’s office got the documents to TAS, a referral then went to the IRS, and in just a few short weeks, the Dunlops’ refund of more than $22,500 was in the mail.
- Kevin Noah of Vernon: Kevin filed his federal tax return, and eight months went by without a word from the IRS. When the agency finally asked for additional documentation, it was documentation he could no longer get his hands on. Kevin reached out to Gottheimer’s office. His team contacted TAS and followed up to explain Kevin’s situation, including that his wife, Maryellen, had stopped working in January and that he had become her primary caregiver after she was hospitalized. In less than a month, Kevin’s refund of more than $7,000 was released. From his first call to a refund in hand, it took about a month. Kevin put it best: “This is how the government is supposed to work.”
- David Mitnick of Glen Rock: David and his wife, Shelly Berger-Mitnick, reached out to Gottheimer’s office for help with their federal tax refund and a penalty abatement request. After the IRS audited them and found them ineligible for the energy tax credit they listed, they learned they were actually eligible for the credit in the following year. David repaid the previous year’s federal income tax amount in full, requested a penalty abatement, and filed an amended return, but after more than eight months, no refund or decision came. Gottheimer’s office contacted TAS right away and worked with David and their CPA to get TAS the forms and documents it asked for. Two months after they first called, the IRS confirmed $4,427.59 for their penalty abatement and $20,413.78 for their federal tax refund, more than $24,800 in total was sent to them.
If you are experiencing an issue with a federal agency, Gottheimer and his Constituent Services Team are here to listen and help with VA benefits, Social Security, Medicare, passports, delayed IRS refunds, and more. Reach out to Gottheimer in Fair Lawn at 201-389-1100, by email at HelpNJ5@mail.house.gov, or visit Gottheimer.House.Gov for more information and resources.
